primitives.name: Atomic Commit Semantics
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Writes: each `create_commit` is **atomic** (all add/delete/copy ops in one call succeed or fail together), but there is **no server-side lock across commits** — concurrent pushes to the same branch race, last-writer-wins.
primitives.assumptions: All operations within a single commit are applied atomically; concurrent commits may conflict.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When multiple agents write to the same branch, last-writer-wins behavior occurs.

layer2.mapping: Commit semantics mirror transactional consistency in distributed systems, ensuring data integrity.
layer2.telemetry: Commit success/failure rates, race condition frequency.

The HF Hub functions as a Git-based data lake where datasets are stored as repositories, enabling versioning, branching, and full history tracking. Each dataset repository behaves like a Git repository with LFS support for large files, allowing for immutable data shards that are ideal for backtesting and calibration. Concurrent reads are unlimited and served via CDN, while writes are atomic but subject to last-writer-wins conflicts when not coordinated. Agent token scoping provides fine-grained access control, enabling secure multi-agent collaboration without credential sharing. Atomic commit semantics ensure data consistency during updates, though concurrent writes introduce potential races. These primitives form a coherent foundation for scalable, reproducible, and secure agent-based data workflows.
